newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains prices ease, wheat could fall on.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains prices ease, wheat could fall on.

text.p: Most grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) eased further on Friday and uncertain export outlooks were seen depressing wheat prices further, traders said.
"Rail transport capacities might limit (wheat) exports to some 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
The Agriculture Ministry forecast a five million tonne wheat crop and with domestic demand below three million tonnes, that would leave two million tonnes for export.
Wheat futures have been declining for the last two weeks and traders said further falls are likely but the spread will be reduced.
"There is little room for significant downward movement of nearby maturities but the more distant ones could lose more," Szoke said.
On Friday, milling wheat fell 40 to 310 forints per tonne for most positions, with May the biggest loser, ending at 24,500 forints compared with Thursday's 24,810.
Nearby July rose 290 forints on position-squaring while August and March remained flat.
Szoke said feed barley prices would have followed falling milling wheat futures were it not for July position-squaring.
Trendless maize futures dropped 100 to 230 forints for October, November and March, were flat for December, May and July 1998 while nearby July went limit-up to 20,800 forints.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was 1,183 lots or 503.68 million forints, little changed from Thursday's 1,141 lots or 488.49 million forints.
